newsitem.title: UK: London palladium fixed at $235.00, fresh high.
newsitem.headline: London palladium fixed at $235.00, fresh high.

text.p: Palladium prices jumped to a fresh all-time high fixing on Thursday and platinum reached its highest fix in nearly two years as dealers scrambled for metal.
Palladium fixed at $235.00 per ounce, up from $208.00 on Wednesday, and its sister metal platinum fixed at $440.00, its highest level since September 15, 1995.
It was palladium's highest fixing since the twice-daily official fixing system began in 1989 and the metal's highest spot price since early 1980.

"Things are very tight in the spot market. A big U.S. hedge fund is holding 1.5 million ounces and who knows when this will come on the market. Every participant who is short in palladium is being forced to borrow," a dealer said.
"It can't be sustainable at current levels. The industry won't accept this high level and will have to think of some substitutes," he added.

Palladium and platinum are both used in electronics, chemical processes and in the autocatalysts which remove noxious gases from car exhaust fumes. Palladium is also used in dental alloys and platinum in jewellery
